summary: {{confirmed}} confirmed, {{probable}} probable and {{review}} to review ({{scanned}} definitions read).
outside: Only what is in the database is visible: applications, reports and external scripts that use it do not appear here.
unreadable: The definition of {{names}} could not be read. Whatever depends on the object there is not in the list.
none: Nothing in the database depends on this object.
usesNone: It doesn't use other objects in the database.

relationUses.foreign_key: Tables its foreign keys point to
relationUses.code: Tables, views and routines its code names

confidenceTip.confirmed: The engine's catalog records the dependency.
confidenceTip.probable: The object's code names the object (and the column, with its table).
confidenceTip.review: The name appears inside a text, probably dynamic SQL: you have to read it to know whether it uses it.

lineage.hint: Click: details · double-click: open · + on the sides: one more level
lineage.capped: The diagram reached {{n}} objects and adds no more: open the lineage of one of them to continue from there.

cross.switchTip: Shows what reads this object from other connections: the Power BI tables fed by it and, from there, their models, reports and dashboards.
cross.nobody: No other connection reads this object.
cross.reader: This Power BI item reads the object.
cross.many: Several connections match this source. Pick one: the same one is used next time.
cross.remembered: The choice is remembered; "Unlink" removes it.
cross.none: No saved connection matches this source.
cross.notFound: This object was not found in {{name}}.
cross.userPrompt: User to connect to {{source}}. The connection is temporary and read-only: it isn't saved.
cross.loginIntro: To see its lineage you need to connect to {{source}}. The connection is read-only.
cross.loginNote: The connection belongs to the lineage and does not appear in the explorer. The password goes to the system keychain only if the box stays checked.
cross.noServer: This source is not a server DBine can connect to.

ask.text: This engine has no dependency query in its catalog: to draw the lineage, the definitions of the database's views, routines and triggers have to be read and searched for the objects they name. On a large database it can take a while.

database.overview: The database has {{objects}} objects in {{schemas}} schemas: an overview by schema is shown, and each line's thickness is the number of dependencies crossing it. A click on a schema shows its detail and a double click expands it.
database.truncated: The database has more objects than were read, so the diagram is incomplete. Open the lineage of a schema or a kind to see it whole.
database.hidden: The diagram shows only the first cards: {{hidden}} objects are missing. Collapse a schema or use the filters.
database.empty: There are no objects to draw in this scope.
database.relationsTip: Foreign keys (and a model's relationships) run in parallel to the lineage: turn them on to see them along with it.

sources.title: Lineage sources
sources.intro: Connections the lineage made on its own to follow a source to another database (for example, the SQL Server table a Power BI model reads). They do not appear in the explorer. You can forget them or add them to the explorer as regular connections, which stay read-only.
sources.none: There are none yet: they are created when you follow a source in a lineage.
sources.notRemembered: No password remembered: asked every session
sources.forgetConfirm: The connection "{{name}}" and its remembered password are removed. The lineage asks again the next time it follows that source.
sources.internalNote: The lineage's own connection: "{{name}}" is not in the explorer.
